kept.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via require()
kept.description: The function `loadQueries` in `node.js` uses `require.resolve` and `require` on user-controlled input (`name`) passed from the Browserslist query `extends`. An attacker who can influence the config file or the `extends` query can force the application to load and execute arbitrary JavaScript code present on the filesystem.
steps_to_exploit: Find an entry point that processes a browserslist config or accepts an `extends` query.
Craft a query or a configuration file that uses `extends <malicious_path>`.
Place a malicious JavaScript file at the specified path or point to an existing sensitive file.
The application executes the code via `require()`.
kept.impact: Full RCE (Remote Code Execution) on the server running the build process.

kept.title: Insecure Path Traversal in File Reading
kept.description: Various functions like `readConfig` and `findConfig` in `node.js` resolve and read files based on user-provided path segments. While some checks exist, they are insufficient to prevent access to arbitrary files if the base directory or environment variables are manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate the environment variable `BROWSERSLIST_ROOT_PATH` or supply crafted input to `findConfig`.
Provide path segments containing directory traversal characters (e.g., ../).
The application reads sensitive files (like /etc/passwd or configuration files) when expected to only read project-local configs.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to arbitrary sensitive files on the server.

kept.title: Use of Dangerous Environment Variables in Workflow
kept.description: The CI workflow sets `ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true`, which re-enables deprecated and dangerous workflow commands that can be exploited for command injection if an attacker compromises a dependency or repository file.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a PR that modifies a file processed during the workflow (like `package.json`).
Inject a malicious command that triggers the insecure workflow syntax.
The runner executes the injected command with elevated CI permissions.
kept.impact: CI/CD pipeline compromise, potentially exposing secrets or altering build artifacts.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution in Object Copying
kept.description: The `copyObject` function manually filters specific keys, but the implementation is vulnerable to bypasses if nested objects are passed or if the environment allows different prototype accessors, potentially leading to property injection.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a JSON input that utilizes advanced prototype accessors not covered by `DANGEROUS_KEYS`.
Pass the object to a function that performs deep operations on the merged object.
Pollute the global `Object.prototype` to alter application logic.
kept.impact: Application-wide state manipulation or potential denial of service.

kept.title: Deserialization of Untrusted JSON with `readFileSync`
kept.description: The `cli.js` reads and parses JSON files provided via the `--stats` command-line argument without schema validation, allowing potential memory exhaustion or unexpected behavior if the input file is large or malicious.
steps_to_exploit: Create a massive JSON file or a JSON file with deeply nested structures.
Run the `browserslist` CLI with `--stats=<path_to_file>`.
The application crashes due to resource exhaustion during `JSON.parse`.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) of the build-time CLI tool.

kept.title: Insufficient Validation of Input in `parseConfig`
kept.description: The `parseConfig` function processes string input using regular expressions to split and extract configuration sections. The lack of strict escaping allows for injection of malicious configuration tokens.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a config string with unexpected newline and `#` characters to manipulate internal logic.
Inject duplicate or hidden sections that override intended configuration.
The tool uses the poisoned configuration to generate browser lists.

kept.title: Exposed Internal Debugging Options in CI
kept.description: The code uses environment variables like `BROWSERSLIST_TRACE_WARNING` and `BROWSERSLIST_DANGEROUS_EXTEND` which, if accidentally set in a production environment, can leak path details or disable security checks.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the `oldDataWarning` condition by forcing the internal state.
Set `BROWSERSLIST_TRACE_WARNING` in the environment.
The application outputs stack traces and sensitive path information to `stdout`.

kept.title: Insecure `node` Version Management in CI
kept.description: The CI workflow uses insecure `pnpm/setup` and `actions/setup-node` versions without fixed commit hashes for all steps or with deprecated/unsecure configurations for early Node versions.
steps_to_exploit: Intercept the network traffic during build time to serve a compromised node binary.
The CI pipeline installs the malicious version without hash verification.
The build environment is compromised.
kept.impact: Compromised build environments leading to supply chain attacks.

kept.title: Potential Command Injection via `exec` (Implicit)
kept.description: The CLI and internal utilities interact with external files and path logic. If any upstream dependency or future implementation introduces child process execution, these paths could be weaponized.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a file path that includes shell metacharacters.
Trigger an operation that passes this path to a shell-executing function (e.g., via `require.resolve` or `fs` interaction).
Commands execute in the environment context.

kept.title: Weak Error Handling Leading to Information Disclosure
kept.description: Errors in `node.js` often include full file paths and details about why a file could not be read, which are directly bubbled up to the user or `stderr`.
steps_to_exploit: Attempt to load a configuration from a guessed sensitive path.
The application returns a `BrowserslistError` revealing the full absolute path of the failure, confirming the file's existence.
Use this for blind path enumeration.

evidence.quote: throw new BrowserslistError("Can't read " + file + ' config')

kept.title: Insecure use of `eval`-like behavior in `parse`
kept.description: The parser logic recursively flattens and processes queries. The way strings are tokenized and processed against regex lists could be abused for ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a specially designed, long, nested query string.
Submit it to the `browserslist` function.
The regex matching logic in `parse.js` enters catastrophic backtracking, consuming CPU and blocking the thread.

kept.title: Use of `var` and Mutable Globals
kept.description: The codebase uses `var` throughout, which allows variable hoisting and re-declaration. Global-like states (`browserslist.data`, `cache`) are mutable and can be tampered with by other loaded modules in the same runtime process.
steps_to_exploit: Require `browserslist` in a shared environment.
Access `browserslist.data` directly and mutate it.
All subsequent calls to `browserslist()` return tampered browser support data.
kept.impact: Integrity compromise of the tool's core logic.

kept.title: Reliance on `caniuse-lite` data integrity
kept.description: The tool trusts the data provided by `caniuse-lite` implicitly. If that package is compromised, the tool will propagate malicious/incorrect browser support information to all dependent build tools (Autoprefixer, etc.).
steps_to_exploit: Compromise the `caniuse-lite` npm package.
Inject a malicious browser support flag that causes breakage or security flaws in the generated output.
Users of `browserslist` automatically pull in the compromised data.
kept.impact: Widespread supply chain vulnerability affecting front-end development tools.

kept.title: Missing Authorization on Custom Usage Stats
kept.description: The feature `loadStat` allows loading a `browserslist-stats.json` file from any path. There is no restriction to ensure the stats file is truly owned or authorized by the project requesting it.
steps_to_exploit: Place a `browserslist-stats.json` in a shared temp directory.
Point the CLI `--stats` argument to this file.
The tool uses arbitrary statistics, potentially forcing the project to adopt insecure/deprecated browser support.

kept.title: Insecure Handling of `package.json` data
kept.description: The `parsePackage` function uses `JSON.parse` on content read from `package.json`. If the package file is malformed or intentionally designed to mimic a browserslist config, it may trigger unexpected errors or state transitions.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a malformed `browserslist` property into a `package.json` file.
The tool fails in a way that leaks path details via the `BrowserslistError` constructor.
Adversary gains insight into the project structure.
